| `POST .../resources` | List the server's resources |
| `POST .../resources/read` | Read one resource by URI |
| `POST .../ex
port` | One JSON snapshot of tools, resources, and prompts |\n| `GET`, `PUT`, `PATCH`, `DELETE .../accounts[/{account}]` | The ser
ver's accounts. See [Server accounts](#server-accounts) |\n| `POST .../oauth/import-tokens` | **Deprecated.** Uploads to your defa
ult account; use `PUT .../accounts/{account}`. See [The deprecated import route](#the-deprecated-import-route) |\n\n**Eval runs**

(`/projects/{projectId}/...`):

| Endpoint | What it does |
| - | - |
| `POST .../eval-suites` | Author-only: create a suite +
its test cases from `name` + `serverIds` + a default `model` + `tests`, WITHOUT running it; responds `201` + `suiteId`. Each test
's case body is an ordered `steps` array (prompt / toolCall / interact / assert); per-test `model`/`provider`/`runs` are optional
and fall back to suite defaults |\n| `POST .../eval-runs` | Create a run from a `suiteId` (rerun; `serverIds` optional — defaults
to the suite's saved servers) or `suiteName` + inline `tests` + `serverIds` (new suite). `environmentId` (requires `suiteId`) runs
against one of the suite's attached environments instead. Responds `202` + `runId` |\n| `PATCH .../eval-suites/{suiteId}` | Edit
suite settings, including `environmentIds` — the project environments the suite runs against (non-empty array sets/replaces, `null
` clears) |\n| `PATCH .../eval-suites/{suiteId}/schedule` | Enable/disable scheduled runs; `environmentId` pins which environment
they launch |\n| `GET .../eval-runs/{runId}` | Run status, result, and summary — poll until terminal. Carries `gateWaiver`: the au
dited override in force over this run's gate, or `null` |\n| `GET .../eval-runs/{runId}/gate` | The stored suite quality-gate repo
rt for this run (`passed` / `failed` / `non_gateable` / `not_configured`). `not_configured` is a 200 report, never a missing route
. A deployment that predates the evaluator answers `422 FEATURE_NOT_SUPPORTED` |\n| `GET .../eval-runs/{runId}/decision-summary` |
**Start here when a run did not pass.** The canonical run decision contract: the verdict and where it came from, counts labelled
with the population they count, the run's own verdict decision, and per-trial diagnostics with the user-value chain, the first fai
led stage, the failure category, evidence scoped to that stage, and one next action (paginated) |\n| `POST .../eval-runs/{runId}/g
ate-waivers` | Override a **failing** run's release gate until `expiresAt` (required, future, max 30 days out), with a `reason` (r
equired, max 500 chars). Manage tier. Does NOT change the run's `result` — the run keeps its verdict and the waiver is reported al
ongside it. `409` when one is already in force, returning the existing waiver |\n| `GET .../eval-runs/{runId}/gate-waivers` | The
waiver in force over a run, or `null`. Readable by anyone who can view the run |\n| `DELETE .../eval-runs/{runId}/gate-waivers/{wa
iverId}` | Revoke a waiver, putting the gate back. Idempotent — a second call reports the original revocation rather than restampi
ng it |\n| `GET .../eval-runs/{runId}/iterations` | Per-iteration results: tool calls, token usage, latency (paginated) |\n| `GET
.../eval-runs/{runId}/iterations/{iterationId}/trace` | Full trace: messages + expected-vs-actual analysis |\n| `GET .../eval-suit
es/{suiteId}/runs` | Recent runs for a suite, newest first |\n\n**Eval result ingestion** (`/projects/{projectId}/eval-ingest/...`
) — how `@mcpjam/sdk` saves results from eval runs executed outside the platform (local dev, CI). The `{projectId}` segment accept
s the literal `default` for the key org's Default project. Most users never call these directly — set `MCPJAM_API_KEY` and the [SD

K reporter](https://docs.mcpjam.com/sdk/concepts/saving-results.md) does:

| Endpoint | What it does |
| - | - |
| `POST .../e
val-ingest/report` | One-shot: create a run from finished results and finalize it |\n| `POST .../eval-ingest/runs/start` | Chunked
flow: create (or idempotently reuse) a run by `externalRunId` |\n| `POST .../eval-ingest/runs/iterations` | Append an iteration b
atch to a started run |\n| `POST .../eval-ingest/runs/finalize` | Finalize a chunked run (idempotent) |\n| `POST .../eval-ingest/a
rtifacts` | Store one artifact's raw bytes (widget HTML too large to send inline) and return its `storageId` |\n| `POST .../eval-i
ngest/artifacts/upload-url` | Retired. Answers `410 Gone` with `details.code: \"SDK_UPGRADE_REQUIRED\"`. `@mcpjam/sdk` 8.17.0 and
later upload artifacts with `POST .../eval-ingest/artifacts` instead |\n\n**Agent** (`/projects/{projectId}/agent`) — a headless a

ssistant turn for
building conversational surfaces (the MCPJam Slack app is the first consumer):

| Endpoint | What it does |
| - | - |\n| `POST .../agent` | Run ONE assistant turn over a `messages` history (`{role: \"user\"\\|\"assistant\", content}` item
s, max 50 messages × 8 KB each, 96 KB total). The model is pinned server-side and billed to the project. The turn can read project
servers/suites/runs and **create eval suites**; it can NOT start runs — kick those off yourself with `POST .../eval-runs`. Respon
ds synchronously with `reply`, the `toolCalls` it made, `createdResources` (ids + app links), and token `usage`. Capped at 4 concu
rrent turns per organization and \\~90 s wall clock. **Not idempotent — never blind-retry**: dedupe on your own trigger identity,
and on an error response check `details.createdResources` (and, after a lost response, list suites) before retrying, or you'll cre

ate duplicates |

**Studies** (`/projects/{projectId}/studies...`):

| Endpoint | What it does |
| - | - |
| `GET .../studie
s` | List the project's published studies: name, access mode, attached servers, share link |\n| `GET .../studies/{studyId}` | One
study's full read: model, system prompt, tool-approval policy, resolved servers, the environment it publishes, and its insights en

velope. The last two need workspace membership and are **absent** for a share-link visitor, never null |

> [!NOTE]
>
> **Swar
ms and User Testing are enabled per organization.** Everything in the\n> four sections below is behind that gate, enforced server-
side. If it is not\n> on for your organization, the reads generally return empty and every **write**\n> — creating a persona or go
al, launching a run, publishing a study,\n> requesting insights — answers `403` with a message naming the feature, not a\n> `404`

and not a validation error.
>
> Five operations are deliberately outside the gate, because every one of them
> *reduces* exposu
re and spend: cancelling a goal run, unpublishing a\n> study, and archiving a persona, goal or swarm (each one's `DELETE`). An\n>

organization that loses access can still stop what is running and clean up
> what it authored.
>
> Ask us on [Discord](https://

discord.gg/JEnDtz8X6z) if you want it turned on.

**Swarms — authoring** (`/projects/{projectId}/personas...`, `.../goals...`,
`.../swarms...`) — the definitions a swarm run executes. A **persona** is a\nreusable synthetic character; a **goal** is the task
you point one at; a\n**swarm** is an authoring container holding defaults for the goals made\nunder it. Nothing here starts anythi

ng — launching is
`POST .../goals/{goalId}/runs`.

| Endpoint | What it does |
| - | - |
| `GET .../personas` | List the proj
ect's personas |\n| `POST .../personas` | Create a persona (accepts `Idempotency-Key`) |\n| `GET .../personas/{personaId}` | One p
ersona |\n| `PATCH .../personas/{personaId}` | Update a persona. Goals reference it by id, so renaming is safe |\n| `DELETE .../pe
rsonas/{personaId}` | Delete a persona. **409** while goals still reference it |\n| `GET .../goals` | List the project's goals |\n
| `POST .../goals` | Create a goal (accepts `Idempotency-Key`). `personaId` and `swarmId` must be in this project |\n| `GET .../go
als/{goalId}` | One goal |\n| `PATCH .../goals/{goalId}` | Update a goal. `null` CLEARS `environmentIds`; `iterations` and `maxTur
ns` must be sent together |\n| `DELETE .../goals/{goalId}` | **Archive** a goal — existing runs keep pointing at the definition th
ey executed |\n| `GET .../swarms` | List swarm containers |\n| `POST .../swarms` | Create a swarm container (accepts `Idempotency-
Key`) |\n| `GET .../swarms/{swarmId}` | One swarm |\n| `PATCH .../swarms/{swarmId}` | Update the container's defaults. Not a casca
